bodyMarkdown:
## How to Calculate a Systems Engineer Salary

When you’re evaluating a job offer or negotiating a pay rise, understanding how your hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential. For systems engineers in Australia, the starting point is often the **Professional Employees Award 2020** [MA000065], which sets minimum pay rates for professional roles including systems engineers. This guide walks you through the calculation, explains the difference between award rates and the National Minimum Wage, and covers casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

### The 38-Hour Week and the 52-Week Year

Most full-time roles in Australia are based on 38 ordinary hours per week. To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, a systems engineer classified at Level 2 (Experienced professional) under the award earns **$39.77 per hour**. That works out to:

- Weekly: $39.77 × 38 = $1,511.26
- Fortnightly: $1,511.26 × 2 = $3,022.52
- Annual: $1,511.26 × 52 = $78,585.52 (the award lists $78,836, a small rounding difference)

Always check the official award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman for the exact figures. The award provides annual wages that already assume a 38-hour week, so you can also use those directly.

### Award Rates vs. the National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). This applies only to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most systems engineers are covered by the Professional Employees Award, which sets higher minimums. For instance, a Level 1 graduate (3-year degree) starts at $33.71 per hour – well above the national minimum.

If you are a casual systems engineer, you receive a **25% casual loading** on top of the award hourly rate. So a Level 2 casual would earn $39.77 × 1.25 = $49.71 per hour. The loading compensates for not receiving paid leave or other entitlements. Use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page to see how it affects your pay.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must contribute **12% of your ordinary earnings** into a superannuation fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). This is on top of your base salary. For a systems engineer earning $78,836 per year, the super contribution would be $9,460.32. The super guarantee rate is legislated and applies to most employees. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more details.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a **2% Medicare levy** (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For a $78,836 salary, the tax estimate is roughly $14,267 plus $1,577 Medicare, leaving about $62,992 after tax. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a systems engineer on $39.77 per hour, the fortnightly gross is $3,022.52. After tax and Medicare, you might receive around $2,423 per fortnight. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing job offers.

### What the Award Says About Systems Engineers

The Professional Employees Award classifies systems engineers under professional levels. The minimum annual wages (full-time) are:

- Level 1 Graduate (3-year degree): $66,825 ($33.71/hr)
- Level 1 Graduate (4 or 5-year degree): $68,538 ($34.57/hr)
- Level 2 Experienced professional: $78,836 ($39.77/hr)
- Level 3 Senior professional: $86,157 ($43.46/hr)

These are minimums; many employers pay above award. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees are $2,083.70 (May 2026), which equates to about $108,352 per year – well above award rates for experienced professionals.

### Important Notes

- The calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds.
- HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

For a quick estimate of your own pay, try our [timesheet](/). If you need to check award classifications, refer to the [reference tables](/data) on our site.

### Summary

A systems engineer salary can be understood by starting with the award rate, multiplying by 38 hours and 52 weeks, then adding super on top. Whether you are a graduate or an experienced professional, knowing these figures helps you negotiate with confidence. Always verify with the Fair Work Commission and the Fair Work Ombudsman for the most current rates.
